en: cook mince in a little water

does: Cooks minced meat in a splash of water or stock in a pan, stirring and breaking it up, so that it stays tender and fine instead of browning.
how: Put the mince in a pan with a splash of water or stock.
Set it over medium heat and stir, breaking the meat into fine crumbs.
Keep stirring until it has changed colour all through and nearly all the liquid has gone.

cues.text: Fine, even, pale crumbs with only a little liquid left.
The crumbs are tender, not hard or dry.

mistakes.fix: Break it up as soon as it goes in, and keep stirring.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking on until it is dry and grainy.
mistakes.fix: Take it off as soon as it is done and a little liquid is left.

variant_of.differs: Only a splash of liquid is used, and the meat is stirred and broken up until it is nearly gone.
